projects.Description:
Anxiety disorders affect 34% of people in their lifetime, and when left untreated, they are debilitating to the individual and create a large public health burden. Anxiety disorders are estimated to cost $42 billion annually in the United States alone due to medical costs and lost productivity.
One therapy effectively treats this entire class of disorders—exposure therapy.  Exposure therapy is a type of cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) in which patients systematically confront situations that they fear and avoid but are not dangerous. Even though exposure therapy is a first line treatment for anxiety disorders, is more effective than medications, and has the most robust research support of any psychotherapeutic intervention, it is also one of the least used treatments in practice. Fewer than one third of mental health providers use exposure therapy with their anxious patients. Because exposure therapy is severely underutilized by clinicians, the vast majority (>70%) of patients suffering from anxiety cannot access effective treatment and must live with anxiety’s debilitating effects—even though an effective treatment exists.
A major reason that clinicians underutilize exposure therapy–even after receiving training and instruction in exposure—is the perception that exposure therapy is too difficult. Clinicians perceive exposure therapy to be difficult in a number of ways, including:
1. Intellectually: high burden of generating, designing, and tailoring exposure exercises
2. Logistically: time and resources needed to prepare and execute exposure exercises
3. Emotionally: distress associated with observing patients’ distress during exposures
Furthermore, research has found that the more difficult a clinician perceives exposure therapy to be, the less likely that clinician is to use exposure with their patients.

projects.Description:
Currently, Small Things receives orders via email from their partners. Orders should contain the organization name, the requests for items off the Small Things “menu”, and a desired pick-up time. Often, many of these pieces of information are not included or specifically spelled out (ie “give me the same as last time”) in the initial email. Orders are then put into a Google sheet manually by Small Things staff. If items are not available or a pick-up time is already taken, the Small Things staff member will email back the partner and find a time that is not taken.
The Google Sheet tracking orders also inform the daily “pick sheets”, that are used by the warehouse members to organize the pallets for the pickups on that given day. These sheets are commonly printed at the start of the day.
Our goal is to create a web application to automate much of this process by creating a web portal for partners to be able to log in and view/create requests through. To create an order, partners will select the items they need and determine a pickup time from the list of open times displayed to them. On the Small Things staff side, all of these requests will populate in a table that they can quickly verify and approve/modify orders from partners with all pertinent information quickly displayed.

projects.Description:
Kiva came to us with the goal of building an app that would allow them to more quickly approve loans to entrepreneurs around the world. With the recent addition of Kiva Zip, a new Kiva product that allows non-traditional lending institutions (such as churches and schools), Kiva was receiving thousands of loan applications and needed a process by which to crowd-source application reading.
We began by sitting down with a few Kiva members who gave us a detailed spec of what they were hoping the app accomplish. Beyond just reviewing loan applications, the “Crowd-based Due Diligence App” needed to be a useful tool for Kiva administrators and create an effective user experience for volunteers. Some of the key features included:
• Gamification to help incentivize volunteers to continue working
• Document viewer so that each loan application could be viewed as the review was being completed
• Dashboard for administrators to quickly see aggregated statistics per loan application
• Question upvote mechanisms for volunteers to determine what other information would be useful in evaluating the loan
At the end of the semester, we handed the project off to the engineering team of Kiva, who will integrate it with their systems and deploy it in the coming year.
projects.Name: Kiva Crowdsourced Due Diligence App
